_about: The archive, newest first. Each piece becomes its own page. text is a list of paragraphs, or, with "form": "poem", of stanzas whose lines are kept (a line starting with "|" is centred; **bold** and *italic* work). author_url, if given, links the author's name.

pieces.title: The Chameleon
pieces.author: John Coyle
text:
The purple crest that crowns the green chameleon
Appears now, a bright flourish amongst cool green brush.
You realize this thing here does not serve to nothing
Though its master is a secret darker than the mind of man.

pieces.title: Après dîner chez Hegel
pieces.author: John Coyle
text:
|**I**
What were man but in a darkness of the mind?
And what were this full red fruit without
This porcelain bowl of bluest white and clearest blue to bear it?
And what spirit, holy or otherwise, goes, peregrine, between?

|**II**
Consider then this long and noble face, baked
By sun and wizened by the wisdom of the plains.
See it, as you will, tipped by a long feather white and black.
Consider, if you can, its singular singularity
Its place in rank among the mighty sons of Bharat
Its christening by an ingenioso son of something.

|**III**
She is a girl of infinite affections. He, the burning parvenu,
Posits her a whole, her madness and her chastity.
Now at last it can commence, the wild rural rondelay
With the girl, wild with ribbons in her long and wild hair.

pieces.title: Savitr of the Triple Fold
pieces.author: John Coyle
text:
Bright leaves gleam hauntgreen
Bright as second sun.
Astonished, she scrutinizes the third,
The übermenschy,
On oblivious palm.

The way up and the way down
Are one and the same,
In the going.

She lingers in suspension.
Tonight, rolling in her welter,
Licking the one, recurrent wound,
Will she curse a human god?
